subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the major product when HBr adds across propene, according to Markovnikov's rule?
questions.explain: The H adds to the carbon with more H atoms, giving the more stable secondary carbocation and thus 2-bromopropane as the major product.

questions.q: The reaction of a halogenoalkane with hot ethanolic potassium hydroxide gives mainly which product type?
questions.explain: Hot ethanolic KOH favours elimination, removing HX to form an alkene.

questions.q: What is the product of the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol?
questions.explain: Concentrated H2SO4 or hot Al2O3 dehydrates ethanol by eliminating water to form ethene.

questions.q: Termination steps in free-radical substitution are characterised by what?
options: Reaction of an alkane with a radical
Combination of two radicals to form a molecule
questions.explain: Termination removes radicals by combining two of them into a stable molecule, so no new radical is formed.

questions.q: Why is the SN2 mechanism described as bimolecular?
options: It occurs in two distinct steps
The rate depends on both the halogenoalkane and the nucleophile
questions.explain: In SN2 the rate-determining step involves both the halogenoalkane and the nucleophile, so the rate depends on both concentrations.

questions.q: In the free-radical substitution of methane with chlorine, which step is the initiation step?
questions.explain: Initiation is the homolytic fission of the Cl-Cl bond by UV light to form two chlorine radicals.

questions.q: What feature is required for a molecule to be optically active (chiral)?
options: A carbon bonded to four different groups
questions.explain: A chiral centre is a carbon attached to four different groups, giving non-superimposable mirror-image enantiomers.

questions.q: Which reagent and observation correctly identifies a carbon-carbon double bond?
options: Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate
Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror
Bromine water decolourises from orange to colourless
Acidified KMnO4 turns from colourless to purple
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise orange bromine water as bromine adds electrophilically across the double bond.

questions.q: In electrophilic addition of bromine to ethene, the curly arrow showing the first bond formed starts from where?
options: A lone pair on bromine to carbon
The C=C pi electrons to a bromine atom
The Br-Br bonding pair to a carbon
questions.explain: The electron-rich C=C pi bond acts as the nucleophile, attacking and polarising the bromine molecule.

questions.q: Which classification describes the alcohol CH3CH(OH)CH3?
questions.explain: The carbon bearing the OH in propan-2-ol is attached to two other carbon atoms, making it a secondary alcohol.

questions.q: A tertiary halogenoalkane undergoes nucleophilic substitution predominantly by which mechanism?
questions.explain: Tertiary halogenoalkanes form a stable tertiary carbocation, favouring the unimolecular SN1 pathway.

questions.q: Oxidation of a primary alcohol under distillation with limited acidified dichromate gives which product?
questions.explain: Distilling off the product as it forms with limited oxidant stops oxidation at the aldehyde stage.

questions.q: What intermediate forms during the electrophilic addition of HBr to an unsymmetrical alkene?
questions.explain: Addition of H+ to the alkene generates a carbocation intermediate before bromide attacks.

questions.q: Which polymer is formed by addition polymerisation of chloroethene (vinyl chloride)?
questions.explain: Chloroethene monomers add together across their double bonds to form poly(chloroethene), known as PVC.

questions.q: Which type of isomerism is shown by but-2-ene but NOT by but-1-ene?
questions.explain: But-2-ene has two different groups on each doubly-bonded carbon, allowing E/Z isomerism, whereas but-1-ene has two H atoms on the terminal carbon.

questions.q: Which alcohol cannot be oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate(VI)?
questions.explain: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol with no H on the carbon bearing the OH, so it resists oxidation.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of (CH3)2CHCH2OH?
questions.explain: A three-carbon chain with a methyl branch on C2 and OH on C1 is 2-methylpropan-1-ol.

questions.q: Which halogenoalkane is hydrolysed fastest by aqueous silver nitrate?
questions.explain: The C-I bond is the weakest carbon-halogen bond, so it breaks most readily, giving the fastest hydrolysis.

questions.q: What is the product of the complete oxidation of propan-1-ol under reflux with excess acidified dichromate?
questions.explain: Refluxing a primary alcohol with excess oxidant oxidises it past the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid, propanoic acid.

questions.q: Which functional group is present in propanal but not in propanone?
questions.explain: Propanal is an aldehyde with a terminal CHO group, whereas propanone is a ketone with the C=O between two carbons.

questions.q: Reaction of bromoethane with excess ethanolic ammonia ultimately can produce which class of product?
questions.explain: Ammonia acts as a nucleophile substituting the bromide to form ethylamine (and further substituted amines).

questions.q: Which species is the nucleophile in the alkaline hydrolysis of bromoethane?
questions.explain: The hydroxide ion uses its lone pair to attack the electron-deficient carbon, displacing bromide.

questions.q: Which mechanism describes the reaction of an alkene with bromine?
questions.explain: Bromine is polarised by the alkene's pi electrons and adds across the double bond by electrophilic addition.

questions.q: Which statement about SN1 versus SN2 is correct?
options: SN1 has a rate independent of nucleophile concentration
SN2 proceeds via a carbocation intermediate
SN1 is favoured by primary halogenoalkanes
SN2 is favoured by tertiary halogenoalkanes
questions.explain: In SN1 the slow step is ionisation of the halogenoalkane, so the rate is independent of nucleophile concentration.

questions.q: How many structural isomers (including branched) have the molecular formula C4H10?
questions.explain: C4H10 exists as butane and 2-methylpropane (isobutane), giving two structural isomers.

questions.q: Which best describes a pair of enantiomers?
questions.explain: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images that differ only in their effect on plane-polarised light.

questions.q: During the radical chlorination of methane, which is a propagation step?
questions.explain: Propagation steps both consume and regenerate radicals, such as a chlorine radical abstracting an H from methane.

questions.q: Which compound exhibits E/Z isomerism?
questions.explain: 1,2-dichloroethene has two different groups on each carbon of the C=C, so it shows E/Z isomerism.

questions.q: Which compound is a secondary halogenoalkane?
questions.explain: In 2-chloropropane the carbon bearing the chlorine is attached to two other carbon atoms, making it secondary.

questions.q: Which pair are positional isomers?
questions.explain: Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol have the same carbon skeleton and functional group differing only in the position of the OH.
